Charu: just landed!! my flat is empty and the SIM shop closes soon 😅
Rekha: breathe. Take the tram to the mall, there's a shop by the pharmacy. I'll send the exact stop
Rekha: also come Saturday, we're cooking for Ugadi, bring nothing
Charu: really? thank you, I was dreading the first weekend 🥺
Rekha: same when I came. Someone did this for me, so now I do it for you
Charu: what about my colleagues? they keep inviting me to trivia night
Rekha: go!! I love our group but I don't want to only ever go to the dinners from home. trivia sounds fun
Charu: ok. trivia Thursday, Ugadi Saturday
Rekha: perfect. and next year you'll help the next newcomer 🙂

How does Charu feel about the first weekend, and what changes it?

qa.q: How can Charu enjoy the group from home and still avoid living in a bubble?
qa.a: Go to the Ugadi cooking on Saturday and also say yes to the colleagues' trivia night on Thursday.

qa.q: Why might Rekha push Charu toward trivia night instead of only the group dinners?
qa.a: Rekha loves the group but does not want to only ever go to the dinners from home, and wants Charu to mix with colleagues too rather than stay in a bubble.

grounding: People from your region are a lifeline; enjoy it but mix with the wider community, and pay forward the help you got to the next newcomer.

subtopic: Moving abroad or to a new city
passage:
Dear Jahnavi,

Welcome to Dubai! Your uncle told me you landed last week and are staying in Karama. When I arrived three years ago, the Telugu association found me a room, lent me a winter jacket for the office AC, and fed me pulihora at every festival. I owe them a lot, so here is my turn.

Some tips: the metro card works on buses too. The Friday market near the creek has proper vegetables. Our group meets for Ugadi next month; come.

But I'll also say what someone should have told me. For my first year, all my friends were Telugu. It was comfortable, and it kept me small. Now I play football with a Filipino and Egyptian team on Tuesdays, and I've learnt more from them than from any year before.

So come for pulihora. Then go find people who've never tasted it.

Call me anytime.
Deepak

qa.q: What did Deepak feel about the help the Telugu association gave?
qa.a: Deepak felt grateful and indebted, wanting to pass the help on to Jahnavi.

qa.q: What balance does Deepak recommend, and why?
qa.a: Enjoying the Telugu group's food and festivals while also mixing with the wider community, because staying only in the group kept Deepak small.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi feel receiving this letter?
qa.a: Jahnavi may feel welcomed and less alone in a new city, with practical tips and a friendly contact.

grounding: The letter shows someone for whom people from their region became a lifeline, paying that help forward while urging the newcomer to mix with the wider community too.

subtopic: Moving abroad or to a new city
passage:
"Madhuri, you want to know how I survived Berlin? Let me tell you. I'm Kiran, and I arrived with one suitcase and zero German.

The Tamil group saved me. Seriously. Someone met me at the station. Someone else found my first flat. At Pongal, forty of us crammed into a church hall and I cried into my sakkarai pongal.

But after a year I realised I only spoke Tamil or English, only ate Tamil food, only went to Tamil events. I'd moved to Germany and was living in Chennai.

So I joined a hiking club. Terrible German at first. They laughed at my accent and then taught me the right words. Now I have friends from four countries.

And last month a new student from Madurai messaged the group, lost and scared. I picked her up from the airport. That felt like closing a circle.

Stay close to our people. Just don't stop there."

qa.q: What did Kiran join after the first year?
What was Kiran feeling at the crowded Pongal gathering?
qa.a: Kiran felt emotional and grateful, crying into the sakkarai pongal after being helped so much.

qa.q: What choices helped Kiran avoid staying in a bubble?
qa.a: Joining the hiking club, learning German, making friends from four countries, and helping the new student from Madurai.

qa.q: How might the new student from Madurai have seen Kiran's airport pickup?
qa.a: She likely felt relieved and less scared to have someone from her region meet her.

grounding: The spoken account shows someone for whom fellow migrants were a lifeline, who then mixes with the wider community and pays the help forward to a newcomer.
